statement.p: Find the equation of the tangent line to the curve x^4 + y^4 = 97 at the point (3, 2).

static.solution:
Solution:
First use implicit differentiation to find the derivative. \begin{array}{rcl} \dfrac{d}{dx}[x^4 + y^4] \amp =\amp \dfrac{d}{dx}[97]\\ \amp \amp \\ 4x^3 + 4y^3y' \amp =\amp 0\\ \amp \amp \\ y' \amp =\amp \dfrac{-4x^3}{4y^3} = -\dfrac{x^3}{y^3} \end{array} Plug in (x = 3\) (y = 2\) get the slope. m = -\dfrac{(3)^3}{(2)^3} = 3.375 Then use point-slope form to find the equation of the tangent line. y - 2 = 3.375(x - 3) \; \textrm{or,} \; y = 3.375 x - 8.125
